memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "there also I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by my glory. So I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar and will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests." - Exodus 29:43-44 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God says the place will be consecrated by His glory. Not by the craftsmanship, not by the gold, not even by the sacrifices themselves — by His glory. What made the tabernacle holy was God's presence in it. Without Him it was expensive fabric and metal in a desert.

Notice too who does the consecrating. "I will consecrate the tent... and will consecrate Aaron and his sons." Moses performed the ceremonies, but God did the actual setting apart. Human hands went through the motions; divine presence accomplished the reality.

That is a relief. We cannot make ourselves holy by our rituals, however sincerely performed. Holiness is God's work in us, not our achievement before Him. Paul prays that the God of peace Himself would sanctify us through and through (1 Thess 5:23), adding that the One who calls us is faithful and will do it. What makes your life holy is not your religious effort but God's presence within you. Ask Him today to fill the ordinary structure of your life with His glory.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to manufacture holiness rather than asking God to work it in me?
What ordinary part of my life needs God's presence to make it holy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, only Your presence makes anything holy. I cannot manufacture holiness by my effort. Fill the ordinary structure of my life with Your glory and set me apart for Yourself. Amen.
